page: Amazon Web Services r5.12xlarge is a memory-optimized server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with an x86_64 architecture, offering 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz and includes a 35 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark data indicates that the r5.12xlarge delivers average multi-core processing and memory performance, while single-core performance is relatively weak. In multi-core tests, the server achieved average ratings in stress-ng multi-core CPU and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory bandwidth tests, both cached and uncached, also fall into the average category, with uncached read bandwidth reaching 110.33 GB/sec. Single-threaded tasks, such as gzip compression and Geekbench single-core tests, consistently rank in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-core throughput, the r5.12xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-thread performance or local NVMe storage. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and memory-heavy enterprise applications. The 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth supports moderate data transfer requirements. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded processing or large-scale LLM inference, where its performance is weak.
